Move gradually and smoothly only when safe, then cancel the turn signal.

title.text: Manage road transitions and emotional readiness

why_how.text: If not already in the exit-side lane, signal and move toward it about half a mile before the freeway exit.
Signal before entering the deceleration lane, then slow there without disrupting freeway traffic flow.
Adjust speed to any posted exit-ramp speed while traveling through the ramp.
After leaving a freeway ramp, stay alert and adapt to the new road's conditions and slower speeds.
Safe driving requires knowing and following road rules and proper procedures, with courtesy and consideration for others.
Mental and physical condition can affect driving performance.
Remain patient in heavy traffic, avoid hurried last-second decisions and rely on personal alertness rather than other drivers' signals.
If emotionally upset, have someone else drive.
Worry, distraction and overconfidence can interfere with safe, alert driving.
Concentrate on driving rather than daydreaming, shopping from the car, intense conversation or scenery.

why_how.text: Safe driving requires continuous attention so changes can be seen and answered in time.
Talking on a phone or texting can distract a driver and contribute to a crash.
Eating, reading or writing while driving can divert attention from the road.
Changing radio settings or lighting a cigarette can distract from driving.
Applying makeup or shaving can distract the driver.
Searching inside the vehicle or dealing with children or pets can draw attention away from driving.
Even a few seconds of distraction can hide a child entering from between parked cars, a cyclist crossing the path or sudden braking ahead.
Preset radio stations and load recorded audio before driving.
Keep audio low enough to hear outside warnings, including sirens, horns and tire noise.
A front-seat passenger can handle navigation from maps or a phone; a solo driver should learn the route before entering the vehicle.
Do not eat while driving.
Teach children appropriate in-car behavior so tending them does not take attention from the road.
Use a pet carrier to prevent pets from causing problems during the drive.
If lost in thought and inattentive, pull to the roadside and stop for a break.
Park in a safe place before making a phone call or exchanging text messages.

title.text: Respond to fatigue and unattended-vehicle risk

why_how.text: When drowsy, stop driving, leave the highway at the first rest stop or service area and take a nap.
Do not depend on stimulants or energy drinks to keep driving while sleepy; the handbook warns they can increase danger.
Highway hypnosis is drowsiness associated with monotony and the steady noise of wind and tires.
On long drives, shift visual attention among roadway areas and objects at differing distances and to both sides.
An unattended vehicle in a highway's traveled portion may be towed immediately at any time.
An unattended vehicle off the traveled lanes but on the highway's paved portion must be removed before dark or may be towed at the owner's expense.
